title: Update pricing & packaging docs for AWS/GCP Marketplace SKUs (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
author: Elliot Price
release_notes: Docs only: refresh packaging/pricing guidance for Marketplace SKUs; clarify Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private purchase paths; add buyer-facing SKU mapping table (non-pricing) and Marketplace billing FAQ.
commits: docs(marketplace): add Marketplace SKU overview + purchase-path decision tree
docs(packaging): update Hosted/Dedicated/Private pages to reference Marketplace SKUs and entitlements
docs(faq): add Marketplace billing & procurement FAQ and support routing
docs(nav): update IA + add redirects for legacy marketplace URLs
description:
Summary: This PR updates the public docs pricing/packaging guidance to reflect the new Marketplace SKU catalog (v2) and to make purchase paths explicit for buyers coming from AWS/GCP Marketplace. The goal is to reduce confusion between Hosted API usage-based SKUs, Dedicated capacity reservations, and Private deployments, while keeping the docs free of hard-coded price points (Marketplace pricing remains authoritative in the partner portals and private offers).

Key changes (content): Added a Marketplace Overview page that explains (1) subscription → (2) entitlement → (3) Redwood org provisioning/linking → (4) API key creation → (5) metering/invoicing. Updated the existing Hosted / Dedicated / Private pricing pages to include a “Buying via Marketplace” section with clear callouts: Hosted = usage-based metering; Dedicated = capacity reservation/commit (SLA-backed) and not a per-token SKU; Private = platform license + support tier and typically requires a sales-assisted flow (often via private offer). Added a buyer-facing SKU mapping table (names + what’s included + what’s not included) without listing dollar amounts; the table is intentionally phrased as “dimensions you will see on invoices” rather than “plans.” Added an FAQ focused on procurement and billing semantics: what gets billed in Marketplace vs directly by Redwood, entitlement propagation delays, credits/trials policy wording, and support routing for provisioning issues.

Key changes (IA / navigation): Added Marketplace section to the left nav and linked it from the Pricing overview page. Added redirects for legacy Marketplace URLs referenced in older partner submissions (requested in INT-771) and updated internal links in existing onboarding docs to point to the canonical Marketplace landing page.

Wording / compliance constraints: Per PMM + Finance review, we avoid stating specific price points, discount policies, or minimums, and instead direct users to Marketplace listing pricing / private offer terms. Per Security review, we kept security statements scoped and consistent with the Marketplace security packet language (encryption, audit logs, retention). Any “SOC 2” references are phrased as posture/availability of reports via established channels, not public disclosure.

Acceptance checklist: (1) No hard-coded pricing numbers in docs. (2) Marketplace SKU names match the current catalog naming conventions and do not conflict across AWS/GCP. (3) Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private purchase path is unambiguous on first read. (4) FAQ answers map to Support macros and don’t create new commitments. (5) Redirects validated for the URLs supplied by Partnerships.

Validation: Ran full build + link-check locally and in CI. Verified redirects for the legacy Marketplace doc slugs and updated any remaining references. Spot-checked the SKU table renders correctly on mobile and does not wrap awkwardly.

Notes for reviewers: Please focus on (a) whether the Dedicated vs Private distinction is clear enough for procurement-led readers, (b) whether Marketplace billing language is accurate for both AWS and GCP, and (c) whether any phrasing could be interpreted as a contractual commitment. References used: Marketplace SKU catalog v2 (internal), Marketplace offer structure notes (AWS/GCP), and the current Marketplace onboarding flow spec. Follow-ups: A separate PR will update screenshots/visual assets once Design finalizes the listing screenshot plan.
